messages:
maria: heads up — noticed a ~12-18ms p99 host-side latency bump on canary after the kernel-selector change landed. trace shows most of the extra time in tokenization + request parse path.

sam: can you paste the pprof/top output? is it CPU or syscall bound?

maria: CPU-bound mostly, but there are more `writev` syscalls in the hot path now. pprof heap/cpu:

```
pprof: top 10
  26.3%  runtime.(*mSpan).free
  19.8%  github.com/redwood/inference/host/tokenizer.TokenizePrefix
  14.2%  github.com/redwood/inference/host/parse.RequestUnmarshal
  11.1%  net.(*conn).Write
   9.5%  sys_writev
   6.4%  github.com/redwood/inference/serving/kernel.SelectKernels
   5.0%  github.com/redwood/inference/host/streaming.chunkAndEmit
```

maria: attaching a trimmed flame sample (copied inline): TOKENIZE -> UNMARSHAL -> WRITEV -> KERNEL_SELECT slowpath. Also saw a cold-start spike when kvcache misses happen for new prefixes.

jon: interesting — kernel selector change added per-request heuristics that probe sequence length distributions. that probe allocates a small slice per request, might explain the mSpan/free churn.

anya: +1 on allocations. we enabled the adaptive kernel probing (PR #2431) which stores short-lived meta objects. if kvcache miss triggers, we now do extra validation which touched tokenization boundaries.

lee: on the writev side: the change switched from coalesced buffer -> multiple iovecs for streaming to reduce latency in ideal case, but when requests are small it increased syscall count. can we re-coalesce for host-proxy path?

maria: proposed triage: 1) revert adaptive-probe for canary to confirm it's the cause. 2) add pooled buffers for tokenize/unmarshal to avoid mSpan churn. 3) change streaming backend to prefer single big buffer for host-proxy path when seq_len < 512. 4) adjust kvcache cold-start backoff to pre-warm prefixes seen in routing logs.

sam: agree. quick repro: run `wrk -t8 -c200 --script small_chat.lua http://gateway/call` with token lengths ~120. I can run a microbenchmark with and without PR to measure delta.

jon: i've started an allocation flame with `go test -cpuprofile` on the canary image. dropping the adaptive probe reduced allocs by ~22% in local. pushing a revert now?

maria: please hold on revert until we have the benchmark. if it is the probe we can also switch to a sync.Pool-backed object instead of full revert.

deploy-bot: canary deploy 2026-03-12T14:02:31 started for service=host-proxy image=host-proxy:canary-4572

anya: small patch landing to reuse token buffers: https://git.internal/r/redwood/host/+/4589 — it replaces `make([]byte, 0, N)` sites with pool.Get/Put. should reduce mSpan activity.

lee: i'll put in a heuristics change: re-coalesce streaming iovecs when total payload < 8KB. that should cut writev count without losing streaming benefits for large outputs.

sam: ran the wrk repro: baseline canary with patches shows p99 down from 128ms -> 112ms (host-side part). still above original baseline (pre-PR) which is ~95ms. so buffer pool + iovec coalesce helps but kernel probe still shows 6% CPU.

maria: next steps: 1) monitor canary for 4h after patches, 2) if steady -> promote to stable. 3) if p99 > +10% rollback the probe. jon, can you add a quick metric for kernel-selector probe hits (tagged by reason) so we can see frequency?

jon: will add a telemetry counter and a debug histogram for sequence-length buckets. ETA 2h.

infra-bot: alert created: HOST-PROXY-LATENCY-CANARY — ping eng-runtime, thresholds breached at p99+10%

maria: thanks all. logging follow-ups: (a) add trace annotation when kvcache miss leads to probe path, (b) add debug log when we choose iovecs>1 in host-proxy stream so we can correlate with writev spikes.

anya: filing follow-up ticket: INF-1192 "kernel-probe alloc churn + streaming iovecs -> host p99" with triage steps and benchmark results.

lee: quick note — re-coalesce patch is cheap, pushing now to canary; if telemetry improves we'll avoid a full revert.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: host-proxy:canary-4589 -> success (instances: 3)
